ESIGN/FOOTER/DESC: Internal use — Elections Canada Electronic Signature Service
ESIGN/HOME/DESC: Track your signature requests and open a service below.
ESIGN/STEP1/DESC: Start from an approved Nintex AssureSign template or upload your document.
ESIGN/STEP2/DESC: Set the signing order, authentication, and language for each recipient.
ESIGN/STEP3/DESC: Recipients are notified and sign securely from any device.
ESIGN/STEP4/DESC: Follow signing progress in real time and retrieve the completed, audited documents.
ESIGN/FEATURE1/DESC: Initiate signature requests from approved templates and track signing progress in real time.
ESIGN/FEATURE2/DESC: Upload documents once and re-use them as Nintex AssureSign templates across your team.
ESIGN/FEATURE3/DESC: Every signature event is logged with a tamper-evident audit trail meeting GC Protected B standards.
ESIGN/ENVELOPES/DESC: Create and manage electronic signature envelopes.
ESIGN/TEMPLATES/DESC: Browse approved signature templates. Use one to send an envelope, or download the source document.
ESIGN/NOTIF/SUB: Messages and alerts about your envelopes, templates and documents.
ESIGN/ACT/SUB: A combined record of your envelopes, templates, documents and notifications.
ESIGN/HELP/SUB: Everything you need to send, sign and manage documents with the Electronic Signature Service.
ESIGN/BRIEF/SUB: A secure, GC-compliant way to send, sign and manage documents — built on the Nintex AssureSign platform and Microsoft Power Platform.
ESIGN/BRIEF/WHAT/B: The Electronic Signature Service lets Elections Canada teams request legally binding signatures on official documents without printing, scanning or mailing. Envelopes are created from approved templates, routed to signers in order, and tracked to completion with a tamper-evident audit trail.
ESIGN/BRIEF/SEC/B: All data is held in Dataverse within the Elections Canada tenant. Access is governed by Entra ID and Power Pages table permissions. Every signature event is logged, and completed documents carry a verifiable audit certificate meeting Government of Canada IT security standards.
